title: Registered response, but PUT absent from retained operation map
explanation: The response body is registered, but this operation has no retained resource association. The listener therefore never reaches its request. ApiManagement demonstrates same-name registration overwrite; absence from the map is proven for every target, not an assertion that every absence has the same decorator cause. TypeSpec rule update required: cover the actual PUT operation rather than relying solely on a singular retained registration slot; add overwritten-alias controls. title: Genuine plain-response 200/201 mismatch
source:
@tag("QuotaInformation")
  @Azure.Core.useFinalStateVia("original-uri")
  createOrUpdate is ArmResourceCreateOrReplaceAsync<
    CurrentQuotaLimitBase,
    QuotaPutBaseParam,
    Response =
      | ArmResourceUpdatedResponse<CurrentQuotaLimitBase>
      | ArmCreatedResponse<
          QuotaRequestSubmitResponse201,
          ExtraHeaders = ArmLroLocationHeader<FinalResult = CurrentQuotaLimitBase> &
            Azure.Core.Foundations.RetryAfterHeader
        >,
    Error = ExceptionResponse
  >;
explanation: Quota returns CurrentQuotaLimitBase for 200 and QuotaRequestSubmitResponse201 for 201. Only the canonical registered resource is a response candidate; the plain nonresource 201 body is ignored.
